criteria.text: Given the Command Center, when it is opened, then every tab is reachable and every card drills down one level.
criteria.evidence: tests/browser-walk.js: all 9 tabs reachable; 65 cards each open their own page

criteria.text: Given sample mode, when any tab is shown, then the sample data is visibly labelled as sample.
criteria.evidence: tests/browser-walk.js: sample banner on every tab and a Sample tag on every card; none in Real mode

criteria.text: Given the Command Center, when any tab renders, then .colaberry/plan.json and .colaberry/progress.json are both committed in this repo and every tab reads its content from them at runtime rather than from hard-coded values.
criteria.evidence: assets/js/data.js loads the files at runtime; tests/browser-walk.js removes STORY-003 from plan.json and it disappears from the page

criteria.text: Given the Command Center, when any tab is shown, then .colaberry/manifest.json is committed in this repo and every tab shows how old that data is and warns when the age exceeds a week.
criteria.evidence: assets/js/main.js stamp on every tab; tests/browser-walk.js serves a manifest 9 days old and every tab warns

criteria.text: Trust — no tab shows a number, a connection or a result the project has not actually produced.
criteria.evidence: Systems grey and "Not checked from here"; agents "No runs recorded"; no dates shown because plan.json has none; tests/browser-walk.js checks each

stories.notes: All nine tabs built after the Overview review. Every criterion checked against the repo on 2026-11-11 with 11 unit tests and a browser walk (9 tabs, 65 cards, sample labels, stale-data warning, deleted story, missing file, phone width). plan.json still carries no dates, so the Gantt uses plan weeks and no due dates are shown.

criteria.text: Given a user has an issue, when they report it via the help desk, then they receive assistance.
Given a resolved issue, when the user checks the status, then it shows as resolved.
Trust: All help desk interactions are logged for audit.

stories.notes: A user reports an issue and is told at once who has it, by when, and which help articles match. Status shows resolved once support resolves it; a wrong fix is reopened. Every write goes through a hash-chained audit log and is saved together with its audit line or not at all.

criteria.text: Given the system is running, when monitoring is active, then performance metrics are displayed.
Given a system outage, when it occurs, then an alert is generated.
Trust: All monitoring data is archived for audit.

stories.notes: Real checks of the site with a 5 s time limit and one retry record availability and response time. An outage opens one incident and raises an alert; recovery resolves it. Samples are append-only and the archive downloads with its SHA-256.

criteria.text: Given system data, when a report is generated, then it reflects current performance.
Given a report request, when data is missing, then an error is shown.
Trust: Reports are archived for future reference.

stories.notes: A report is computed at generation from the samples, incidents and tickets of the period. A period with no monitoring data is refused with an error naming what is missing. Reports are stored once, cannot be edited, and carry the SHA-256 of their body, checked when opened.

criteria.text: Given user feedback, when a feature is developed, then it meets user needs.
Given a feature request, when it is not feasible, then feedback is provided.
Trust: All feature changes are documented.

stories.notes: Feedback is assessed: feasible becomes a FeatureChange (proposed, approved, in build, released) that cannot be released without a recorded check of how it meets the feedback; not feasible is declined with the reason shown to the submitter. Every change step is in the audit log and the change history.

criteria.text: Given new features, when training is conducted, then staff understand functionalities.
Given a training session, when a user misses it, then a recording is available.
Trust: Training completion is logged.

stories.notes: Sessions are scheduled with their materials (optionally linked to the feature they teach), and cannot be marked held without a recording. A person completes training only by passing the knowledge check (80%), live or from the recording, so completion means understanding. Every attempt and completion is logged; completing the cyber security course records the date on the person (REQ-020).

criteria.text: Given a report request, when generated, then it meets specifications.
Given a report error, when it occurs, then it is logged and addressed.
Trust: All reports are archived for compliance.

stories.notes: Reports are built section by section from recorded data and checked against their specification before archiving. A report that cannot meet it (no data for a required section, or a source system not connected, such as the TxDOT financial system) is refused and logged as an incident, which is addressed by a later successful run or by hand with the cause. Archived reports are unchangeable and carry the SHA-256 of their body.

criteria.text: Given a compliance check, when conducted, then no violations are found.
Given a legal update, when it occurs, then the system is updated accordingly.
Trust: Compliance checks are logged.

stories.notes: A register of 14 federal and Texas rules (compiled from official sources, to be confirmed by TxDOT legal) is checked rule by rule: mechanical checks run against the live store (vendor cyber training, audit controls, retention, an automated accessibility scan); rules about records this build does not hold are not applicable, with that reason. A run on the workspace finds no violations. A legal update raises the rule version and re-checks it at once; older checks show as stale. Every check is logged with its evidence.

criteria.text: Given a response, when submitted, then it is stored correctly.
Given a submission error, when it occurs, then it is logged and addressed.
Trust: All submissions are tracked for audit.

stories.notes: A response is checked before anything is stored (on time, every required document, accepted files), then every file is stored and read back by hash and the response is saved with its documents and a SHA-256 receipt. A failed submission is logged as an incident and addressed by a later valid submission or by hand. Every submission and status change is tracked in the audit log. Euna Procurement is not connected, so tracking is in the workspace.

criteria.text: Given a response, when evaluated, then it is scored accurately.
Given a scoring error, when it occurs, then it is corrected.
Trust: All scores are archived for transparency.

stories.notes: Criteria with weights totalling 100; each evaluator scores each criterion 0 to 10; weighted score = sum of weight x mean / 10, tested against hand calculation. A score more than 4 points from the other evaluators is flagged; corrections are new scores that name the one they replace and why, so nothing is overwritten. The ranking and every score are archived with SHA-256 for transparency.

criteria.text: Given a risk assessment, when conducted, then risks are identified and mitigated.
Given a risk, when it is not mitigated, then it is logged for review.
Trust: All risk assessments are archived.

stories.notes: An assessment reads the live system for outages (open incidents, availability under 99%), slow performance, user error (reopened tickets, failed checks), operator error (late or overdue maintenance, report errors) and security gaps (lapsed cyber training, compliance violations). Each finding is a Risk with likelihood, impact, score, evidence, owner and mitigation plan; risks are mitigated when the condition is gone or the owner records the action; score-9 or overdue open risks are logged for review. Every assessment is archived with SHA-256.

criteria.text: Given a cybersecurity training, when completed, then compliance is ensured.
Given a security breach, when it occurs, then it is logged and addressed.
Trust: All training completions are archived.

outstanding: Given a cybersecurity training, when completed, then compliance is ensured.

Trust: All training completions are archived.

criteria.text: Given the system is operational, when a technical issue arises, then the support team must resolve it within the SLA.
Given a maintenance schedule, when maintenance is due, then the system must undergo maintenance without disrupting services.
Trust: All support and maintenance activities must be logged and auditable.

stories.notes: Every open ticket is tracked against its service level (on track, at risk, breached, met, missed). Maintenance can only be scheduled outside service hours and without overlaps; a window past its end and not done shows as overdue. On-duty changes and maintenance are logged.

criteria.text: Given a new document, when it is uploaded, then it must be stored in the document management system.
Given a stored document, when it is accessed, then it must be retrievable within 2 seconds.
Trust: All document access and modifications must be logged.

stories.notes: Documents are uploaded by category, hashed, stored (IndexedDB in the browser) and read back before the upload counts. Opening a document is timed against the 2 second target and checked against its hash. Only compliance, procurement, contract-manager and administrator roles may upload or open; refusals are logged. Every upload, replacement, opening and refusal is in the audit log.

Given user actions, when an error is made, then the system must provide corrective suggestions.
Trust: All anomalies and user errors must be logged for audit purposes.

Trust: All reports and assessments must be version-controlled and logged.
